key_insight: Introduce a region-graph guided optimal-transport routing that assigns WSI patches to specialised experts, preventing routing collapse and enabling experts to adapt to local pathological heterogeneity for improved whole-slide classification.
problem_solved: Addresses weak specialization and unbalanced routing in Mixture-of-Experts MIL for gigapixel whole-slide images, where a single shared pathway or unconstrained softmax routing fails to capture spatially varying pathology and causes expert underuse or collapse.
method: Construct a region-graph over WSI patches that encodes spatial proximity and local context to group related instances.
Use optimal-transport based routing to assign patch groups to experts with balance and locality constraints, promoting specialization while avoiding highly imbalanced softmax routing.
Train expert subnetworks to process their routed regions and aggregate expert outputs for slide-level prediction, using routing regularizers to enforce specialization and interpretability.
impact: Enables more accurate, robust and interpretable WSI classification by letting experts focus on spatially coherent pathological patterns while preventing expert collapse and load imbalance — useful for scalable clinical-grade MIL systems.

paper_title: Region-Graph Optimal Transport Routing for Mixture-of-Experts Whole-Slide Image Classification
paper_authors: Xin Tian, Jiuliu Lu, Ephraim Tsalik, Bart Wanders, Colleen Knoth
